items.title: 68002_Benny Waters oral history interview
items.q: I took Dicky Wells' place in Switzerland with Bill Coleman... Dicky Wells was working with Bill Coleman at the point... So I had a chance to join him on account of Dicky Wells just got tired and left.

ctx.x: From the very beginning at Jimmy Ryan's on 52nd Street, when Jimmy says 'We're going to Europe', my vision was Paris. Do you know when I got to Paris - Jimmy never did play Paris - I got to Paris with Bill Coleman, see what I'm talkin' about, that's clear, that's the same way. But I, when the big Paris opened, Paris was somethin' else, I wanted to go to Paris, you see? I said maybe I'll go to Paris, I wish that I could go to Par-, you und-, you follow what I mean now? I hope that I'll go to Paris. I didn't,…

items.title: 68002_Benny Waters oral history interview
items.q: We had more advanced musicians in it, you know what mean? ... Dickie Wells and Sidney de Paris

ctx.x: Billy Taylor was one of the greatest of the bass players I ever heard, bass horn, you know. I'm working in a great band, that was just some extry money. So when those guys in Europe says "Did you really work with King Oliver?" I could, I would get sarcastic and told 'em that "No", like I got tired of answering the question, you know what I mean?
